terms.name: Blinded
terms.summary: You can't see. Attacks against you have advantage, your own attacks have disadvantage, and any ability check that needs sight fails.

terms.name: Charmed
terms.summary: You can't attack the creature that charmed you or target it with harmful abilities or magic, and it has advantage on ability checks to interact socially with you.

terms.name: Deafened
terms.summary: You can't hear, and any ability check that needs hearing fails.

terms.name: Exhaustion
terms.summary: Comes in six levels, each adding a penalty to those before it: disadvantage on ability checks at level 1, up to death at level 6. Finishing a long rest with food and drink removes one level.

terms.name: Frightened
terms.summary: While the source of your fear is in sight you have disadvantage on ability checks and attack rolls, and you can't willingly move closer to it.

terms.name: Grappled
terms.summary: Your speed is 0. It ends if the grappler is incapacitated or something moves you out of its reach.

terms.name: Incapacitated
terms.summary: You can't take actions or reactions.

terms.name: Invisible
terms.summary: You can't be seen without magic or a special sense. Attacks against you have disadvantage, and your attacks have advantage.

terms.name: Paralyzed
terms.summary: You are incapacitated and can't move or speak. You automatically fail Strength and Dexterity saving throws, attacks against you have advantage, and any hit from within 5 feet is a critical hit.

terms.name: Petrified
terms.summary: You are turned to stone: incapacitated, unaware of your surroundings and resistant to all damage. Attacks against you have advantage, and you automatically fail Strength and Dexterity saving throws.

terms.name: Poisoned
terms.summary: You have disadvantage on attack rolls and ability checks.

terms.name: Prone
terms.summary: You are on the ground and can only crawl until you stand up, which costs half your speed. Your attacks have disadvantage; attacks against you have advantage from within 5 feet and disadvantage from farther away.

terms.name: Restrained
terms.summary: Your speed is 0. Attacks against you have advantage, and you have disadvantage on attack rolls and Dexterity saving throws.

terms.name: Stunned
terms.summary: You are incapacitated, can't move and can speak only falteringly. You automatically fail Strength and Dexterity saving throws, and attacks against you have advantage.

terms.name: Unconscious
terms.summary: You are incapacitated, can't move or speak, drop what you're holding and fall prone. You automatically fail Strength and Dexterity saving throws, attacks against you have advantage, and any hit from within 5 feet is a critical hit.

terms.name: Concentration
terms.summary: Some spells last only while you concentrate on them, and you can concentrate on one spell at a time. When you take damage, make a Constitution saving throw (DC 10 or half the damage, whichever is higher) or the spell ends.

terms.name: Surprised
terms.summary: If you're surprised when a fight starts, you can't move or take an action on your first turn, and you can't take a reaction until that turn ends.

terms.name: Attack
terms.summary: Make one melee or ranged attack, or more with a feature such as Extra Attack.

terms.name: Cast a Spell
terms.summary: Cast a spell whose casting time is 1 action.

terms.name: Dash
terms.summary: Gain extra movement equal to your speed for this turn.

terms.name: Disengage
terms.summary: Your movement doesn't provoke opportunity attacks for the rest of the turn.

terms.name: Dodge
terms.summary: Until your next turn, attacks against you have disadvantage if you can see the attacker, and you make Dexterity saving throws with advantage.

terms.name: Help
terms.summary: Give an ally advantage on their next ability check for a task you help with, or on their next attack against a creature within 5 feet of you.

terms.name: Hide
terms.summary: Make a Dexterity (Stealth) check to try to hide.

terms.name: Ready
terms.summary: Choose a trigger and an action or a move. If the trigger happens before your next turn, you can use your reaction to do it.

terms.name: Search
terms.summary: Spend your action looking for something, usually with a Wisdom (Perception) or Intelligence (Investigation) check.

terms.name: Use an Object
terms.summary: Use an object that takes an action, or interact with a second object on your turn.

terms.name: Grapple
terms.summary: In place of one attack, try to seize a creature no more than one size larger than you: your Strength (Athletics) check against its Strength (Athletics) or Dexterity (Acrobatics). If you win, it is grappled.

terms.name: Shove
terms.summary: In place of one attack, push a creature no more than one size larger than you 5 feet away or knock it prone: your Strength (Athletics) check against its Strength (Athletics) or Dexterity (Acrobatics).

terms.name: Opportunity Attack
terms.summary: When a hostile creature you can see moves out of your reach, you can use your reaction to make one melee attack against it.

terms.name: Two-Weapon Fighting
terms.summary: When you attack with a light melee weapon in one hand, you can use a bonus action to attack with a light melee weapon in the other. You don't add your ability modifier to that attack's damage unless it is negative.

terms.name: Stabilize
terms.summary: Use your action and a DC 10 Wisdom (Medicine) check to stabilize a creature at 0 hit points, so it stops making death saving throws.

terms.name: Darkvision
terms.summary: Within its range you see in dim light as if it were bright light, and in darkness as if it were dim light, though only in shades of gray.

terms.name: Passive Perception
terms.summary: 10 plus your Wisdom (Perception) modifier, with +5 for advantage or -5 for disadvantage. The DM uses it to decide whether you notice something without rolling.

terms.name: Action
terms.summary: The main thing you do on your turn, such as Attack, Cast a Spell, Dash or Dodge. You get one action each turn, as well as your movement.

terms.name: Bonus Action
terms.summary: A quick extra action on your turn, available only when a feature, spell or other ability says it takes a bonus action. You get one each turn.

terms.name: Reaction
terms.summary: An instant response to a trigger, which can happen on someone else's turn, such as an opportunity attack. You get one, and it comes back at the start of your turn.

terms.name: Initiative
terms.summary: A Dexterity check everyone rolls when a fight starts. Turns then go from the highest total to the lowest.

terms.name: Attack Roll
terms.summary: A d20 roll to hit, plus your ability modifier and your proficiency bonus if you're proficient with the weapon (always, for a spell). You hit if the total equals or beats the target's Armor Class. A natural 20 always hits and a natural 1 always misses.

terms.name: Melee Attack
terms.summary: An attack against a target within your reach, usually 5 feet.

terms.name: Ranged Attack
terms.summary: An attack at a distance. You have disadvantage beyond the normal range or when a hostile creature that can see you is within 5 feet, and can't attack beyond the long range.

terms.name: Armor Class
terms.summary: How hard you are to hit. An attack hits you if its total equals or beats your AC.

terms.name: Critical Hit
terms.summary: Rolling a 20 on the d20 for an attack. It hits, and you roll all of the attack's damage dice twice, then add your modifiers as normal.

terms.name: Hit Points
terms.summary: How much harm you can take. Damage lowers them and healing restores them, up to your hit point maximum. At 0 you fall unconscious and start making death saving throws.

terms.name: Temporary Hit Points
terms.summary: A buffer that takes damage before your real hit points. They don't add up: if you gain more, keep whichever amount you like. Healing can't restore them, and they last until used up or you finish a long rest unless a feature says otherwise.

terms.name: Resistance and Vulnerability
terms.summary: Resistance to a damage type halves the damage you take of that type; vulnerability doubles it. Immunity means you take none.

terms.name: Death Saving Throw
terms.summary: At 0 hit points, roll a d20 at the start of each of your turns: 10 or higher is a success. Three successes make you stable and three failures mean death. A 1 counts as two failures, and a 20 brings you back with 1 hit point.

terms.name: Cover
terms.summary: Obstacles between you and an attacker protect you. Half cover gives +2 to AC and Dexterity saving throws, three-quarters cover +5, and total cover means you can't be targeted directly.

terms.name: Difficult Terrain
terms.summary: Ground such as rubble, undergrowth or deep snow. Every foot you move through it costs an extra foot of movement.

terms.name: Advantage and Disadvantage
terms.summary: With advantage, roll two d20s and use the higher; with disadvantage, use the lower. If you have both, they cancel out and you roll one d20.

terms.name: Proficiency Bonus
terms.summary: A bonus, +2 at 1st level rising to +6 at 17th, that you add to attack rolls, ability checks and saving throws made with things you're proficient in. It is never added to the same roll twice.

terms.name: Ability Check
terms.summary: A d20 roll to see whether you succeed at a task: add the ability's modifier, plus your proficiency bonus if a skill or tool you're proficient with applies, and meet or beat the DC.

terms.name: Saving Throw
terms.summary: A d20 roll to resist a spell, trap or other danger: add the named ability's modifier, plus your proficiency bonus if you're proficient in that save, and succeed if you meet or beat the DC.

terms.name: Difficulty Class
terms.summary: The number an ability check or saving throw has to equal or beat to succeed. A spell's DC is its caster's spell save DC.

terms.name: Short Rest
terms.summary: At least an hour of light activity. You can spend Hit Dice to regain hit points, and some features, such as a Warlock's spell slots, come back.

terms.name: Long Rest
terms.summary: At least 8 hours, mostly asleep. You regain all your hit points and up to half your Hit Dice, and most features and spell slots come back. You can finish only one in 24 hours.

terms.name: Hit Dice
terms.summary: One die per level, its size set by your class (a d10 for a Fighter, for example). In a short rest you can roll them to regain hit points, adding your Constitution modifier to each; a long rest gives back up to half of them.

terms.name: Inspiration
terms.summary: A reward the DM gives for playing your character well. Spend it to gain advantage on one attack roll, saving throw or ability check. You either have it or you don't: it never stacks.

terms.name: Ability Score Improvement
terms.summary: At certain class levels you increase one ability score by 2, or two scores by 1 each, to no more than 20. If your DM allows feats, you can take a feat instead.

terms.name: Spell Slot
terms.summary: What you spend to cast a spell of 1st level or higher. Each slot has a level, and a spell can use a slot of its own level or higher. Spent slots come back when you finish a long rest, or a short rest for a Warlock.

terms.name: Spell Level
terms.summary: How powerful a spell is, from 0 (cantrips) to 9. Casting it takes a slot of at least that level. It isn't the same as your character level.

terms.name: Cantrip
terms.summary: A 0-level spell you can cast at will, without a spell slot. Many cantrips get stronger as your character level rises.

terms.name: Prepared Spells
terms.summary: The spells you have ready to cast, chosen from your class's spell list, or for a Wizard from your spellbook. Clerics, Druids, Paladins and Wizards can change their prepared spells after a long rest.

terms.name: Spells Known
terms.summary: Bards, Rangers, Sorcerers and Warlocks know a set number of spells and can cast any of them. They usually swap one for another only when they gain a level.

terms.name: Spellbook
terms.summary: A Wizard's book of spells. Wizards prepare their spells from it each day, and can copy new wizard spells they find into it.

terms.name: Ritual
terms.summary: A spell with the ritual tag can be cast as a ritual: it takes 10 minutes longer and uses no spell slot. Only a class or feat with ritual casting lets you do this.

terms.name: Spell Save DC
terms.summary: The number a target's saving throw must equal or beat to resist your spell: 8 + your proficiency bonus + your spellcasting ability modifier.

terms.name: Spell Attack Bonus
terms.summary: What you add to the d20 when a spell makes an attack roll: your proficiency bonus + your spellcasting ability modifier.

terms.name: Spellcasting Ability
terms.summary: The ability your class casts with: Intelligence for Wizards, Wisdom for Clerics, Druids and Rangers, Charisma for Bards, Paladins, Sorcerers and Warlocks. It sets your spell save DC and spell attack bonus.

terms.name: Components
terms.summary: What casting a spell needs: V (verbal, speaking), S (somatic, gestures with a free hand) and M (material, particular items). A component pouch or spellcasting focus can stand in for materials that have no cost.
